title: Status Page Update SLA & Cadence (by Severity)
author: Tomáš Novák
body:
## Purpose
This page defines Redwood Inference’s customer-facing **status page update SLAs** and **recommended cadence** during incidents. The goal is consistent, timely, and actionable communication across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private offerings—without overpromising or disclosing sensitive details.

This is a comms standard. It does **not** change incident severities, roles, or internal response requirements; it ensures customers get predictable updates that reflect what we know at the time.

## Scope
Applies to all incidents where customer impact is possible or confirmed, including:
- Hosted API (chat/text, streaming, embeddings, rerank)
- Console (dashboard access, usage, keys)
- Dedicated (serving, reserved pools, control plane actions)
- Private (VPC/on-prem control plane actions, customer-managed networking)

## Definitions
**Status page update phases** (customer-facing): Investigating → Identified → Monitoring → Resolved.

**Time to First Update (TTFU):** Time from incident declaration (internal) to first public status page update.

**Next update time:** A timestamp communicated in each update indicating when the next update will be posted (or earlier).

**Customer impact language:** Use the approved terms and examples in “Customer Impact Classification” (e.g., “Degraded performance”, “Partial outage”, “Outage”), and name the affected components/regions.

## Roles & ownership
### Required roles for customer-facing updates
- **Incident Commander (IC)**: Accountable for ensuring updates are posted on time.
- **Comms Owner (CO)**: The person writing and publishing status updates. By default this is the IC unless explicitly delegated.
- **Tech Lead (TL)**: Provides confirmed technical details (scope, mitigation, progress) to the Comms Owner.
- **Support Liaison (optional but recommended for Sev0/Sev1)**: Ensures Support macros and customer escalations match the status page.

### Default ownership rules
- If the incident is declared by Eng/SRE: **IC owns** meeting TTFU and cadence; IC may delegate to an SRE or a designated Comms Owner.
- If declared by Support/CS escalation: SRE on-call assumes IC/CO responsibilities as soon as the incident is accepted.
- If multiple components/regions are impacted, **one incident** should still have a single Comms Owner (avoid split messaging).

## SLA and cadence by severity
> These are minimum standards. Post sooner if there is meaningful new information or if customer confusion is likely.

### Summary table
| Severity | Typical external label | Time to First Update (TTFU) | Ongoing cadence (Investigating/Identified) | Monitoring cadence | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Sev0** | Outage / Major outage | **≤ 10 minutes** | **Every 20 minutes** (or sooner) | Every 30–60 minutes | Ensure next-update timestamp is always present; engage Support liaison immediately. |
| **Sev1** | Partial outage / Degraded performance | **≤ 15 minutes** | **Every 30 minutes** (or sooner) | Every 60 minutes | Prefer component + region specificity (e.g., Streaming in us-east). |
| **Sev2** | Degraded performance / Minor impact | **≤ 30 minutes** | **Every 60 minutes** | Every 2–4 hours | If impact is limited to a subset of customers/models, state that clearly. |
| **Sev3** | Advisory / No confirmed impact | **≤ 2 hours** (or not required; see below) | As-needed (when new info) | N/A | Use status page only if customers are likely to notice; otherwise rely on internal comms. |

### Sev3 guidance (when to post vs. not)
Post a public status page incident for Sev3 when at least one is true:
- Customers are likely to see errors/latency soon (early indicators + credible risk)
- There is known partial impact (even if low volume) but unclear scope
- Support is receiving inbound reports that require a canonical public reference

Do not post for Sev3 when:
- It is purely internal tooling, no customer path impact, and no credible risk
- The only symptom is internal alert noise with no correlated SLO/SLA risk

## What each update must include (minimum bar)
Each status update must include **at least one** of the following, and should include more when known:
1) **Impact**: what is happening in customer terms (component/region + symptom)
2) **Mitigation/Workaround**: what customers can do (retry/backoff, region pinning, fallback model) if applicable
3) **Next update time**: explicit timestamp

Additionally:
- Always select the correct **components** and **regions** (see mapping guidelines).
- Avoid internal jargon (e.g., “scheduler”, “control plane reconciliation”); use customer-friendly terms (e.g., “Capacity & Routing”, “Dedicated Control Plane”).
- Use uncertainty language appropriately: “We are investigating”, “We believe”, “We have identified”, “We have confirmed”.

## Content standards by phase
### Investigating
Use when the issue is not yet confirmed or root cause is unknown.
Include:
- Customer-facing symptoms and scope (component/region/model family if known)
- Confirmation we’re investigating
- Next update time

Avoid:
- Root cause speculation
- Overly broad blast radius (“all customers”) unless confirmed

### Identified
Use when the cause category or failure mode is confirmed and mitigation is underway.
Include:
- What we identified (safe phrasing; no sensitive provider/security details)
- Current mitigation steps (rollback, capacity shift, rate limiting, routing)
- If available: estimated time to improvement (ETI) with careful wording (“We expect”, “We are working toward”)
- Next update time

### Monitoring
Use when the mitigations are in place and metrics show recovery, but we are not ready to close.
Include:
- What improved and what we’re watching
- Any residual risk or remaining affected scope
- Next update time OR criteria for resolution (“If metrics remain stable for X minutes…”) when appropriate

### Resolved
Use when customer impact is fully remediated.
Include:
- Confirmation of resolution
- High-level summary of what happened (1–2 sentences) and mitigation
- Link expectation for post-incident summary (for Sev0/Sev1, and Sev2 when requested)

## Approval workflow (who must review)
### Default publishing authority
- **Sev0 / Sev1:** Comms Owner drafts; **SRE Lead on-call** (or SRE Manager designee) must approve before publish when feasible.
- **Sev2:** Comms Owner can publish; seek SRE Lead review if the update includes non-routine customer guidance or broad impact.
- **Sev3:** No approval required; do not post if it creates confusion.

### When to involve Security/Legal/Compliance before publishing
Engage Security/Legal review **before posting** when the incident involves any of:
- Suspected security event, abusive traffic that changes access patterns, or potential data exposure
- Vulnerability-like behavior or anything that could be weaponized
- A third-party provider event where contractual language restrictions apply
- Any customer-specific details (never name customers publicly)

Escalation contacts (business hours + on-call rotation as applicable):
- Security approver: **Dr. Aisha Rahman**
- Security engineering reviewer: **Marcus Lin**
- Privacy/legal: **Michael Grant**
- Compliance guidance: **Olga Petrov**

If Security/Legal is engaged, do not miss the cadence: publish a safe holding update (“We are investigating an issue affecting …; next update by …”) while review proceeds.

## Overdue update escalation
### Automated reminders
Incident-bot will prompt for:
- Next update time on every publish
- Reminder at **T-5 minutes** before the stated next-update timestamp
- “Overdue” alert at **T+5 minutes** past next-update timestamp

### Human escalation path (when updates are overdue)
If the next update time is missed by more than:
- **5 minutes (Sev0/Sev1)**
- **15 minutes (Sev2)**

Then follow this escalation:
1) Comms Owner posts an immediate short update with (a) current known impact and (b) next update time.
2) Ping **#incidents** and **#eng-oncall** tagging IC + TL: “Status page update overdue; posting holding update now.”
3) If still overdue after an additional 10 minutes (Sev0/Sev1), escalate to:
   - **Rafael Mendes** (SRE Manager) and **Sean Gallagher** (Dir SRE)
4) Notify Support liaison (**Dev Patel** or delegate) to align macros and reduce customer confusion.

Root causes for overdue updates should be captured in the internal postmortem (e.g., role confusion, tooling friction, approval bottlenecks).

## Long-running incidents (multi-hour)
For incidents lasting longer than 2 hours:
- Maintain cadence even if “no new updates”; customers value acknowledgement and a predictable timeline.
- Provide periodic refinement of scope (component/region/model families) as it becomes clearer.
- If mitigation is “in progress” for an extended period, provide what we can safely share: what we tried, what changed, what we’re trying next (without internal or sensitive detail).

## Handling partial degradations and confusing symptoms
Common patterns and how to communicate:
- **Streaming-only failures:** Use the Streaming component(s) rather than broad “API” if non-streaming requests succeed.
- **Region-specific capacity constraints/429s:** Prefer region components (e.g., Hosted API Serving (us-east)) and include customer actions (backoff, region pinning, temporary fallback).
- **Model-family issues:** Name the affected model family in customer terms (e.g., “Llama 3.x family deployments”) if that is actionable and not sensitive; otherwise describe as “a subset of models”.

## Coordination with Support/CS
For Sev0/Sev1 incidents:
- Support macros must reference the status page and must not contradict it.
- If a workaround is posted publicly, ensure Support has it within 5 minutes.
- If the status page cannot include a detail due to disclosure constraints, provide a Support-only guidance note in the incident channel (do not send speculative technical root cause).

## Compliance: what we never publish
Do not include in status page updates:
- Customer names, account identifiers, ticket IDs, or customer-specific timelines
- Exploit details, vulnerability hypotheses, or step-by-step reproduction that could be weaponized
- Provider or partner contractual details, or blame-oriented statements
- Internal service names/hostnames, dashboards, incident room links

Use the approved templates and disclosure policy for safe phrasing.

## Metrics (how we measure adherence)
We track:
- Time to First Update (TTFU) by severity
- % updates with next-update timestamps
- Overdue update count and duration
- Customer follow-ups tagged “what’s impacted?” during incidents (Support)
- Post-incident summary SLA compliance (Sev0/Sev1)
